findings.title: Materials' 121% growth bet is extreme
findings.body: Materials shows a 57-point percentile gap between trailing and forward lenses, the widest in the table, with trailing P/E at the 89th percentile but forward at the 32nd. That implies analysts are underwriting 121 percent earnings growth — a bet that the current earnings collapse is temporary, not structural.

findings.title: Energy's forward discount masks earnings risk
findings.body: Energy's forward P/E sits at the 40th percentile while its trailing multiple is at the 79th, a 39-point gap. The 54 percent implied earnings growth is what makes the forward lens look cheap; if that growth fails to materialize, the trailing valuation is far less forgiving.

findings.title: Industrials' forward richness lacks earnings support
findings.body: Industrials trades at a 32-point percentile gap favoring the forward lens, yet implied earnings growth is only 13 percent — the lowest among sectors with a wide gap. That means the forward multiple is rich not because of expected expansion, but because trailing earnings are depressed; the market is paying up for a modest recovery.
